statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-75803 ("AEAD Forgeries with Empty Ciphertext When Using EVP_Cipher()", Low): when an application finalizes ChaCha20-Poly1305 or AES-OCB decryption of an empty ciphertext by calling EVP_Cipher(), OpenSSL reports success without checking the supplied authentication tag, so an application that relies on that call to verify the tag can accept a forged message. OpenSSL 3.5.0 to 3.5.7 are affected and 3.5.8 is fixed (https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20260825.txt); the fix on the 3.5 branch is https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/bdeb0cd994d915342787f117ee75044f0dc36f34, which makes the built-in OCB and ChaCha20-Poly1305 implementations check the tag on that call and gives ChaCha20-Poly1305 a separate update function. The advisory states that the OpenSSL FIPS modules are not affected, because these algorithms are not implemented in them. The openssl-fips packages built from this source, in the DHI security repository, hold the OpenSSL FIPS provider module (fips.so) and its configuration files; the version string in each build's fips.so, read on x86_64 and aarch64, is the OpenSSL release that the package version names (3.5.5 through 3.5.9). None of those fips.so files contains ChaCha20-Poly1305 or AES-OCB code (the names ChaCha20-Poly1305 and AES-OCB are not found in any of them, while AES-256-GCM is found in each, and the same search finds them in the OpenSSL libcrypto), so those packages are not affected even where the range reads them as affected. The DHI Alpine 3.23 openssl packages are built from the upstream OpenSSL source release that their version names, with Alpine's packaging patches, so 3.5.8-r0 is the first published build that contains the fix. The libcrypto debug symbols in openssl-dbg (x86_64) confirm this: the chacha20_poly1305_update function added by the fix is absent in 3.5.5-r0 through 3.5.7-r1 and present in 3.5.8-r0, with chacha20_poly1305_cipher found in every one of those builds as a control. Every earlier published build (3.5.4-r0 through 3.5.7-r1) is affected.

CVE-2026-75803 ("AEAD Forgeries with Empty Ciphertext When Using EVP_Cipher()", Low): when an application finalizes ChaCha20-Poly1305 or AES-OCB decryption of an empty ciphertext by calling EVP_Cipher(), OpenSSL reports success without checking the supplied authentication tag, so an application that relies on that call to verify the tag can accept a forged message. OpenSSL 3.5.0 to 3.5.7 are affected and 3.5.8 is fixed (https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20260825.txt) by https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/bdeb0cd994d915342787f117ee75044f0dc36f34, which also gives ChaCha20-Poly1305 a separate chacha20_poly1305_update function. The advisory states that the OpenSSL FIPS modules are not affected, because these algorithms are not implemented in them. Debian fixed it for trixie in openssl 3.5.7-1~deb13u2 (DSA-6465-1, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-75803). DHI backported the upstream fix earlier, into the third build of Debian 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 in the DHI Debian repository (the first fixed version in the range), and the later build of that source carries it too; the FIPS builds of 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 in the DHI security repository do not, and they sort above those builds, so the range is affected again from the first of them until 3.5.7-1~deb13u2. Evidence, from the libssl3t64 debug symbols on amd64 and arm64: chacha20_poly1305_update is absent in the first two builds of 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 and in both of its FIPS builds, and present in its third and fourth builds and in every build of 3.5.7-1~deb13u2 and 3.5.7-1~deb13u3, including their FIPS builds, with chacha20_poly1305_cipher found in every file as a control; the disassembly of the provider's aes_ocb_cipher in libcrypto on amd64 likewise shows the added empty-input tag check in the third build of 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 and in 3.5.7-1~deb13u2, and not in the second build of 3.5.6-1~deb13u2; the changelog shipped in libssl3t64 records the backport for those two 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 builds and Debian's own fix under 3.5.7-1~deb13u2. Every build of earlier Debian sources (3.5.5-1~deb13u2 and 3.5.6-1~deb13u1, including their FIPS builds) is affected. The openssl-provider-fips packages built from this source, in the DHI security repository, contain only the FIPS provider module (fips.so) and its documentation. The version string in each build's fips.so, read on amd64 and arm64, is OpenSSL 3.5.5, 3.5.6 or 3.5.7 (matching the Debian source version) in the openssl-provider-fips packages of the non-FIPS builds, and OpenSSL 3.1.2 in those of the FIPS builds; the libssl3t64 packages ship no fips.so. None of those fips.so files contains ChaCha20-Poly1305 or AES-OCB code (the algorithm names are not found in any of them, while AES-256-GCM is found in each, and the same search finds them in libcrypto), so the provider packages are not affected even where the range reads them as affected.
